title: Stalk range of selected integer-labelled extension-by-zero generators
statement: Let $X$ be a topological space, $K,C$ abelian sheaves, $\iota:K\to C$ any morphism, and $\alpha:C\simeq\underline{\mathbb Z}$ an isomorphism to the constant integer sheaf [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Let $n\in\mathbb N$ and, for $i\in\operatorname{Fin}(n)$, let $A_i$ be open and $c_i\in\mathbb N$. Let $g:\bigoplus_i j_{A_i!}\underline{\mathbb Z}\to K$ be any morphism, using extension by zero [def-sc-abelian-open-extension-by-zero]. Assume that the image $s_i$ of the canonical unit section under the $i$th component of $g$ maps under $\alpha\iota$ to the constant section $c_i$ on $A_i$. For any predicate $P$ on the indices let $f_P$ have $i$th component equal to that of $g$ when $P(i)$ holds, and zero otherwise. For every point $x$ and every additive isomorphism $e_x:C_x\simeq\mathbb Z$, the range of $e_x(\iota f_P)_x$ is the additive subgroup generated by $\{c_i\mid x\in A_i,\ P(i)\}$. Stalks here are colimits over open neighborhoods. There is no mono, epi, positivity, bound, or attained-divisor hypothesis.

proof.text: Construct canonical constant-sheaf stalk coordinates. The constant presheaf stalk is the coefficient group because the neighborhood category is connected. Compose that colimit isomorphism with the inverse stalk map of toSheafify, which is an isomorphism. The germ equation sends a constant coefficient to itself.

For x in A_i compose inverse constant-stalk coordinates on A_i with the canonical extension-by-zero stalk isomorphism. Its extension-section germ equation and stalkFunctor_map_germ identify the component map. Apply hsection and hvalue to its unit, obtaining c_i in canonical coordinates. Outside A_i the source stalk is zero. The selected component is the original component or zero by Sigma.ι_desc.

Let S be the subgroup generated by active selected labels. Each such label is in the range by the unit calculation, so closure_le proves S is contained in the range. For the reverse inclusion compose with Z -> Z/S. Each active selected component kills the unit, hence is zero because a homomorphism from the integers is determined by 1. Outside its open the source stalk is zero; an unselected component is zero. The stalk functor preserves the coproduct, so colimit hom_ext makes the whole composite zero. Its kernel is S, proving range containment.

Every additive endomorphism of the integers sends z to alpha(1) times z, so preserves every additive subgroup. Apply this to an automorphism and its inverse to show postcomposition preserves the range. Arbitrary e_x differs from canonical coordinates by such an automorphism, proving the formula.
